title: Normalized universal relations among elementary matrices
statement: Let \(R=\mathbb Z\langle X\rangle\) be the free associative unital ring, augmented to \(\mathbb Z\) by \(X\mapsto0\). Does \(\ker(K_2(R)\to K_2(\mathbb Z))\) vanish? Equivalently, is every universally valid stable elementary matrix relation whose Steinberg lift specializes to the identity under augmentation a consequence of the Steinberg relations? The normalization is necessary; arbitrary constant relations include the nonzero \(K_2(\mathbb Z)\).
status: As of November 2026: resolved in the stated augmented formulation. Vaserstein announces the answer in the March 1972 notebook and the free-ring theorem in \citet[second theorem]{vaserstein1973foundations}; \citet[Theorem 28.1 and Corollary 28.1]{vaserstein1976foundations} gives its precise reduced formulation. The February notebook omits the augmentation condition, so the match is qualified rather than an assertion that every unnormalized relation is trivial. No exact earlier recurrence was found in the supplied prior index.

title: Agreement of the early higher algebraic K-theory constructions
statement: For every associative unital ring \(A\) and every \(n\ge1\), do the stable simplicial constructions of Volodin and Vaserstein and the free-resolution constructions of Swan and Gersten agree naturally with \(\pi_nBGL(A)^+\)? One concrete consequence asked in the notes is the Quillen-theory suspension isomorphism \(K_{n+1}(\Sigma A)\cong K_n(A)\). Polynomial-homotopy Karoubi--Villamayor groups are excluded without additional regularity.
status: As of November 2026: resolved for the specified stable constructions and unital rings. The spring 1972 seminar announcement is documented by \citet[introduction, p.97]{vaserstein1976foundations}; \citet[first theorem]{vaserstein1973foundations} publishes the comparison, with the detailed Quillen and free-resolution arguments in the 1976 paper, \S\S27--29. Record 257's catalogue attribution is conditional and does not create an additional independent priority claim. No exact earlier problem identifier was located in the supplied index.
